newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-STARS BEAT RED WINGS 4-3.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-STARS BEAT RED WINGS 4-3.

text.p: Benoit Hogue scored the tying goal with 46 seconds left in regulation and Mike Kennedy's disputed tally 2:03 into overtime gave the Dallas Stars a wild 4-3 victory over the Detroit Red Wings on Friday.
The goal was Kennedy's first since April 12th.

"I was saving my first goal for a big time," he said. "I knew there was a delayed penalty when I saw the referee's arm go up. I got a nice pass and had a real good chance. When I let the shot go I was mad I didn't get it in, but I managed to get the rebound and slide it in while (the goalie) was down."
Joe Nieuwendyk scored twice for Dallas.
The Stars were without leading scorer Mike Modano for much of the third period after he took a 10-minute misconduct penalty.
The first period featured five goals, four on the power play.

In Washingto, Steve Konowalchuk scored his second goal of the game with 2:03 left in overtime as the Washington Capitals blew a three-goal third-period lead before rebounding for a 5-4 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning.
Washington spoiled the return of Tampa Bay goaltender Daren Puppa, who stopped 20 shots and allowed four goals in his first action since opening night.
Puppa returned after surgery November 11th to remove a herniated disc in his back.
"The way I played yeah obviously," said Puppa when asked if he came back too soon. "But at least I can take a lot of stuff out of the game and work on things. I know what I need to do."
The Lightning took their fourth straight loss and are 1-8 in their last nine games.
